title: Put both relics on one map
summary: The northern and southern radio arcs now share one wide image, with measurement markers you can turn on when you need them.

sections.heading: What you’re looking at
body: The radio view starts with the compact-source-subtracted release image, regridded at native pixel spacing so the two catalog centers lie on a horizontal line. The compass shows north. The default display suppresses low-level fluctuations. Show faint signal changes the display stretch.

Opening Measure the relic separation brings up the matched 135 kpc beam and draws the aperture circles, flux-weighted centers and separation on the map. In PSZ2 G181 the native T50SUB beam is about 19.56 × 19.19 arcseconds. A larger viewer makes the existing samples easier to see. The beam sets the physical resolving power.

sections.heading: The release is bigger than the view
body: The atlas has a corrected 2,083-event merger file and three observed radio pairs. The archived 352-cluster z = 0 catalog has 36 numerical datasets, including masses, radii, cooling time, gas fractions and X-ray and SZ offsets.

The TNG-Cluster release also describes snapshot particles, group catalogs, merger trees and z = 0 projection products around 16 GB per file. A bulk projection file can contain all 352 targets for one quantity and viewing configuration. The first useful download for a clock test is a registered set of data for a single event.

checks.title: Validate the matched maps against saved results
checks.result: The exporter checks hashes and reproduces nine apertures and thresholds per field before writing the cache.

checks.title: Verify the additional HDF5 inventory
checks.result: The local secondary file is 73,984 bytes and has 352 unique halo IDs and 36 datasets. The Data page shows the file fingerprint.
